question.problem:
Let $⟨x,y,z⟩$ be the unique solution of the system of equations below. 

$$
{\begin{aligned}y+z=-1 \\ x+5y+3z=k \\ 7x-3y-z=4\end{aligned}
$$

Given that $z=-3$ and that the determinant of the coefficient matrix is equal to $-16,$ find the value of $k.$
question.worked_solution:
First, let's write the determinant of the coefficients matrix:

$$
\begin{aligned}D=|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 1 \\ 1 & 5 & 3 \\ 7 & -3 & -1\end{aligned}|=-16\end{aligned}
$$

According to Cramer's rule, the value of $z$ is given by $z=\frac{{D}_{z}}{D},$ where

$$
\begin{aligned}{D}_{z}=|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & -1 \\ 1 & 5 & k \\ 7 & -3 & 4\end{aligned}| & =0\cdot |\begin{aligned}5 & k \\ -3 & 4\end{aligned}|-1\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & k \\ 7 & 4\end{aligned}|+(-1)\cdot |\begin{aligned}1 & 5 \\ 7 & -3\end{aligned}| \\  & =0-(4-7k)-(-3-35) \\  & =-4+7k+38 \\  & =7k+34.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we have

$$
z=\frac{{D}_{z}}{D}=\frac{7k+34}{-16}.
$$

From the problem statement, we know that $z=-3.$ So, we can solve for $k$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{7k+34}{-16} & =-3 \\ 7k+34 & =48 \\ 7k & =14 \\ k & =2.\end{aligned}
$$
